## The lab's question, in one line {.smaller}

::: {.eyebrow}
THE THROUGH-LINE
:::

Across very different projects, my lab keeps hitting the same methodological
problem:

> **How do you evaluate an AI system when the ground truth is scarce,
> expensive, or contested?**

Three projects, three different *roles* AI plays in answering it.

::: {.notes}
[~30 sec] Open here. Don't list the projects yet — name the shared problem
first so the three slides feel like one argument, not a portfolio tour.
Transition: "Here's the first role — AI as the thing that *makes* the data."
:::

## Daktari Dx — AI as **data generator** {.smaller}

::: {.eyebrow}
ROLE 1 · DATA GENERATOR
:::

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="55%"}
**The problem:** clinical-AI "data deserts." >90% of clinical AI training
data is from high-income settings; African populations are <3%.

**Daktari Dx:** the platform where we run an **RLEF** approach —
expert clinicians validate AI-generated clinical vignettes *before* they
enter evaluation or training corpora.
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
::: {.callout-note}
### AI's role
Generating *and* filtering synthetic clinical encounters, with expert
feedback as the validation loop.
:::

**Funding / partner:** Gillings Innovation Lab — Kenya pilot launching,
CFK Africa partner site.
:::

::::

::: {.notes}
[~75 sec] Emphasize the validation paradox: you can't check synthetic data
against real data you don't have — so expert judgment *is* the ground truth.
Transition: "In the next project AI isn't the data source — it's the thing
under the microscope."
:::

## AugMed — AI as **subject of study** {.smaller}

::: {.eyebrow}
ROLE 2 · SUBJECT OF STUDY
:::

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="55%"}
**Question:** when clinicians work *with* AI, where does the
physician–AI team actually do better — and where does reliance go wrong?

A methodology for **evaluating AI clinical reasoning** and measuring
asymmetric reliance and heterogeneous response (AIM-AHEAD partnership).
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
::: {.callout-note}
### AI's role
The object of measurement — we study physician–AI complementarity, not
the model alone.
:::

Splitting into two papers: **medical** (PLOS Digital Health, CRC-specific)
and **econ** (Management Science — reliance + heterogeneity framing).
:::

::::

::: {.notes}
[~70 sec] The EPID hook here: "ground truth is contested" — clinical
correctness vs. economic value of a decision aren't the same target.
Transition: "Third role — AI not as data, not as subject, but as
infrastructure for getting at truth that lives in experts' heads."
:::

## Sentinel — AI as **elicitation infrastructure** {.smaller}

::: {.eyebrow}
ROLE 3 · ELICITATION INFRASTRUCTURE
:::

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="55%"}
**Setting:** credence-good markets — quality is hard to observe even
*after* the fact, so expert judgment is the only signal.

**Sentinel** (the lab's information-markets platform): uses AI to
*scale expert elicitation* under uncertainty — a mechanism-design
approach to surfacing dispersed expert knowledge.
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
::: {.callout-note}
### AI's role
Market infrastructure — AI elicits and aggregates expert judgment at
scale, rather than substituting for it.
:::
:::

::::

::: {.notes}
[~70 sec] Keep this tight — it's the least familiar to an EPID audience.
The point is the *pattern*, not the platform internals. Transition into
the synthesis: "Step back and the three line up."
:::

## One problem, three roles {.smaller}

::: {.eyebrow}
SYNTHESIS
:::

| Project | AI's role | Where the "truth" comes from |
|---|---|---|
| **Daktari Dx / RLEF** | Data generator | Expert validation of synthetic data |
| **AugMed** | Subject of study | Contested: clinical vs. economic value |
| **Sentinel** | Elicitation infrastructure | Dispersed expert judgment, aggregated |

::: {.fragment}
The methodological spine is the same in all three: **when ground truth is
scarce or contested, the design problem is how to elicit, validate, and
aggregate expert judgment.**
:::

::: {.notes}
[~60 sec] This is the payoff slide — the repeatable narrative. Land the
fragment line slowly; it's the sentence to reuse in grants and CG
fundraising. Then open for questions.
:::
